title: The Sixteen Principal Stars
author: Joseph G. Dalton
description: The Sixteen Principal Stars, 1824-1948, by Joseph G. Dalton (1898), the American astronomer-astrologer and author of The Spherical Basis of Astrology. A technical work for practising astrologers, it gives tables of the positions (longitude, latitude and declination) of sixteen of the brightest and most astrologically significant fixed stars, such as Aldebaran, Regulus, Spica, Antares and Fomalhaut, calculated for the years 1824 to 1948 with allowance for precession, so that their influence can be included in nativities and directions. Dalton also explains how fixed stars have been used in traditional astrology and how to apply his tables. It reflects the late nineteenth-century effort to put astrology on a more accurate astronomical footing. The text is OCR from a public-domain scan and may contain errors.
